response.rationale: R4 (Rhabdomyosarcoma) is supported by multiple raw spans covering the mass size, color, vascularity, biopsy findings, and subcutaneous lobulated appearance, directly matching the vignette's CT and histology. R5 (Angiosarcoma) also matches vascularity and surface bleeding but lacks the biopsy and lobulated mass spans, making it less complete. R4 is the strongest candidate.

rejected.why: Only one raw span (atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation) is too nonspecific and does not cover vascularity or mass characteristics.
Merkel cell carcinoma is rare in children and the raw spans do not include the vascularity or lobulated mass features; granulomatous inflammation is atypical.
Mycobacterial infection is contradicted by the malignant provisional diagnosis and lacks the vascularity and atypical cells.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis is less likely given the atypical cells and marked vascularity; raw spans do not include the lobulated mass or vascular supply.
